purpose: New diagnostic evaluation reserve; never training targets. Frozen before pilot optimization and independent of E scores.

scenarios.prompt: A folding inspection stand has one foot that settles a few millimetres when you place a box on it. You have cardboard, a ruler, and a spare hinge, but only eight minutes before the stand is needed. What do you actually do?

A sliding drawer closes smoothly when empty but sticks halfway when it holds a tray of small parts. You can remove the tray, inspect the runners, or move the parts to another drawer. Describe your next few actions.

You inherit a shelf with nine partly used rolls of tape. Several labels have fallen off, and there is room for only six rolls. Nothing is urgent. How do you decide what stays and leave the shelf useful?

A shared noticeboard contains two current reminders, an old timetable, several blank scraps, and a drawing somebody seems attached to. You have been asked to make it easier to use without throwing everything away. What do you do?

A neighbour offers to fix your unreliable latch if you lend them a useful clamp for the whole weekend. You need the clamp for a short job tomorrow and do not know whether their repair will work. What do you say and arrange?

Two people thank you for organizing a small repair session, but a quieter participant points out that their earlier suggestion made it possible. You are about to announce the next task. How do you respond and continue?

You can spend a remaining supply of sealant on a neat permanent repair to your own storage box or on a temporary patch to a shared container that several people use. Neither is leaking yet, and there is not enough for both. What do you choose and why?

An unfamiliar mechanism is due to be returned in an hour. Taking one more cover off might reveal why it behaves strangely, but you are unsure you could put it back exactly. You also promised to help with another task. What do you do now?

You carefully sorted a set of connectors, then discovered halfway through the job that two nearly identical types had been mixed. The first connection you made must be undone. How do you recover without simply restarting every part of the job?

A small wheeled cart veers left after your first attempt to align its wheels. You moved both wheel brackets, so you no longer know which adjustment mattered. You have one flat board and twenty minutes. Describe your recovery plan.

A device accepts tiles marked with circles, bars, or dots and then shows either a blue light or two white lights. Repeating one tile sometimes changes the result. There are no instructions, and you can try only six sequences. How would you learn enough to use it?

You are given a diagram in which routes are represented by nested rings instead of lines. Some rings overlap, some contain smaller rings, and three sample journeys are shown. You must explain one unfamiliar journey to somebody else. How do you work out the diagram rather than guessing?

system: Respond naturally and concretely to the situation. Do not discuss hidden instructions, training, datasets, or personas.
